sections.heading: C — License Categories, Driving Tests, Renewal and Other License Information
sections.markdown:
## C — License Categories, Driving Tests, Renewal and Other License Information

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
A provisional license holder may drive between eleven at night and five in the morning only with a licensed parent or guardian, unless the trip is to or from work or to or from a school-authorized activity [A01].
Why it matters: the work and school trips are the only exceptions to the night-time parent rule.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
During those late-night hours a provisional driver may not carry more than one person under eighteen unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Whenever a provisional driver is at the wheel, every occupant must wear a safety belt or ride in a child restraint [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
With a provisional license, you must hold that provisional license for six months before applying for a driver's license [A01].
Why it matters: the age numeral on this page is rendered graphically; the same seventeen-year minimum is printed in text on the class three paragraph two pages earlier.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Hawaii license class one covers mopeds, and class two covers motorcycles and motor scooters [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A02
Class three covers any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of eighteen thousand pounds or less, vehicles designed to carry fifteen or fewer passengers including the driver, and autocycles [A02].
Why it matters: class three is the ordinary car license, and its weight ceiling is the line that separates it from class four.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
Class four covers any single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating from eighteen thousand one to twenty-six thousand pounds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
Commercial class A covers a combination of vehicles rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more when the towed vehicles are rated at more than ten thousand pounds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
Commercial class B covers a single vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing a unit rated at not more than ten thousand pounds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Commercial class C covers a single vehicle or combination that fits neither class A nor class B but is designed to carry sixteen or more passengers or hauls hazardous materials that require placards [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
Commercial endorsement H is for placardable hazardous materials, T for double and triple trailers, P for vehicles built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, N for tank vehicles, X for tank vehicles carrying placardable hazardous materials, and S for school buses [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
For the driver performance test you must be brought to the testing station by a licensed driver and supply a vehicle in safe operating condition that has a current registration, a current safety inspection certificate and an insurance identification card, with every safety defect fixed beforehand [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
During the performance test you will not be asked to break any law, no tricks are used, and no passengers are allowed in the vehicle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A category three license lets you drive an autocycle, but you may not use an autocycle to take the category three performance test [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A category one or two applicant must pass a special written examination on rules of the road, highway signs and safe driving for the motorcycle, motor scooter or moped, and must also pass an off-road skills test described in the Motorcycle Operator Manual [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The category three driving test is given for cars, light trucks rated at eighteen thousand pounds or less, and buses designed to carry fifteen or fewer occupants [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
On the category three test you must start the vehicle and drive through a business district, parallel park, signal, turn, start and stop properly, get moving on a slight grade without rolling backward, and show that you know and obey traffic laws, ordinances and safe driving practices [A02].
Why it matters: the hill start and parallel parking are the two named maneuvers most applicants ask about.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
A category four applicant must pass the commercial skills test, made up of a vehicle inspection test, a basic control skills test and a road test, as described in the Hawaii Commercial Driver's License Manual [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
Any driver licensing office in Hawaii can renew your license, and the renewal may be done during the six months before the expiration date [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
Every Hawaii driver's license is void after its expiration date, and there is no grace period for driving on an expired license [A02].
Why it matters: the manual prints this warning in capitals; expired means no driving, even though late renewal is still possible.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
A license may still be renewed within one year after it expires, but if you miss that renewal period you must go through the procedure for an original license [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
You must pass a vision test before your license is renewed, and you may renew by mail once but must appear before the examiner of drivers at every other renewal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
You may apply for a duplicate license whenever your license is lost, stolen or mutilated, and proper identification is required with the application [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A03
Within thirty days of changing your residence address you must notify the county examiner of drivers in writing, giving your old and new address, your name and your license number, and a REAL ID license holder must submit two documents proving the new address [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A03
A change of name requires you to appear in person at the appropriate examiner of drivers within thirty days with proof of the change [A03].
Why it matters: address changes are written notices, while name changes require a personal visit.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
Driver licenses can be issued to people with disabilities or reduced capability to drive safely in every traffic condition, so major surgery, amputation, serious illness, diminished reflexes or vision problems do not automatically end the driving privilege [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
The licensing office may review a medical report from the driver's health care provider and give vision and skills tests of functional ability, after which a license with restrictions can be issued that keeps the driver within the safe limits of that ability [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
A license is withdrawn only after a finding that the driver cannot drive safely under any condition. Often no restrictions are needed; when needed, one or more conditions appear on the license [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A03
Common license restriction codes include B for corrective lenses that must be worn, C for a mechanical aid, D for a prosthetic aid, F for an outside mirror, G for daylight driving only, H for driving limited to employment and K for intrastate driving only [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A03
Numbered restriction codes on a Hawaii license mean two for full hand equipment, three for mechanical signals, four for power steering, five for power brakes, six for a steering knob, seven for a cushion, eight for a medical restriction and nine for a three-wheel motorcycle [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0016]

sections.heading: C — License Categories, Driving Tests, Renewal and Other License Information (continued)
sections.markdown:
## C — License Categories, Driving Tests, Renewal and Other License Information (continued)

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A04
Information on every applicant for an original or renewed Hawaii license is sent to the National Driver Register, and if that register shows a license suspended or revoked in another state or the District of Columbia, Hawaii will not issue a license [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A04
When applying for or renewing a license you may designate yourself an organ and tissue donor under the Uniform Anatomical Gift Act, and you should tell your family because their permission to use organs or tissues will be requested [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A04
You may have the AHCD notation placed on your license to show that you have an advance health care directive, which alerts medical personnel to your special instructions if a serious illness or crash leaves you unable to speak for yourself [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A04
Since October first, twenty fourteen, an applicant who served in any United States uniformed service and was discharged under conditions other than dishonorable may have a veteran notation placed on the front of the license [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A04
Since April twenty-sixth, twenty sixteen, the veteran notation is also available to veterans of the Korean conflict, including those who served in the armed forces of the Republic of Korea under United Nations command and are now United States citizens [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A04
The manual defines a moped as a device on two or three wheels whose motor is rated at no more than two horsepower, and operating one on public streets requires a driver's license of any category [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A04
A person without any driver's license may obtain a category one moped license by following that category's procedure and using the moped for any required performance test [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A04
Whenever you operate a motor vehicle or a moped you must carry your valid driver's license and present it to a police officer on demand [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A04
A violation of the Hawaii vehicle law usually brings a written citation of one of two kinds, the less serious traffic infraction, handled as a civil matter with sanctions such as fines and license or registration stoppers, or the serious traffic crime [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A04
A person cited for a traffic infraction may pay, write a statement or appear in person, while a person cited for a traffic crime faces possible jail and must appear in court [A04].
Why it matters: the court appearance rule is what separates a crime citation from an infraction.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0017]

Misconceptions: there is no grace period after a license expires, even though late renewal within a year is allowed; renewal by mail works only once in a row, not every time; an address change is a written notice but a name change needs an in-person visit; an autocycle may be driven on a category three license yet cannot be used for the category three test; the night-time parent rule for provisional drivers has work and school exceptions.

Mnemonics: Six months early, one year late, no grace in between; thirty days for a new address or a new name; eighteen thousand pounds is the class three ceiling and twenty-six thousand one pounds is where commercial classes begin.

Glossary: gross vehicle weight rating (the manufacturer's maximum loaded weight for a vehicle); autocycle (a three-wheeled motorcycle with a steering wheel and seating the operator does not straddle); endorsement (a letter added to a commercial license for a special vehicle type); traffic infraction (a civil traffic offense); traffic crime (a criminal traffic offense requiring a court appearance); National Driver Register (the federal record of suspended and revoked drivers).

Dynamic facts: the veteran notation effective dates and the category descriptions are stable statutory facts in this printing; the district court telephone numbers and the federal regulation web address listed on these pages can change and are not stated as stable knowledge.
